findings.title: How the waivable-id set is derived is not pinned
findings.detail: The spec says the code accepts only ids that name an existing waivable `minor`/`nit` finding. It also builds `triage_input.waivable` from "surviving `minor`/`nit` findings with canonical ids". `triage_reviews` returns `{outcome, score, score_only, blocking, advisory, waivable_weight}`, with no explicit waivable list. For a `score_only` result, SPEC-0203 puts every surviving finding in `blocking`. Say that the waivable set is `blocking` (or `blocking + advisory`) filtered to non-synthetic `minor`/`nit` findings, and that `_prepare_run` and `_apply_reviews` use the same helper. Otherwise the prompt list and the validation can drift, and AC3 and AC5 have no single definition to test against.

findings.title: Clamped score can make the predicate overestimate
findings.detail: `score` is `max(0, 100 - Σ)`. When the raw sum exceeds 100, `score + waivable_weight` equals W, which is larger than the real post-waiver score (100 - Σnonwaivable). The triager can then run (and cost $0.5) when waiving everything still cannot reach `pass_score`. This needs about 25 `minor` findings and no `must_fix`, so it is rare and fails safe. Either accept it and add a one-line note, or have `triage_reviews` expose the unclamped nonwaivable score. AC1 lists "hopeless score" as false, which this edge case breaks.

findings.title: Waivers do not persist across loops
findings.detail: `waived` is cleared on every entry into `REVIEWING`. If the triager waives some findings but not enough, the route is `fix`, the next loop re-reviews, and the same subjective findings may reappear and be re-judged, possibly differently. Say whether SPEC-0207 files the waived findings of a `fix` outcome at that moment, before they are cleared. Without that, those waivers are lost when the review is re-entered.

findings.title: Hand-built profile with `review.triager: true` but no `personas.review_triager`
findings.detail: The spec covers a hand-built profile without `review.triager` (off). It does not say what happens when `triager` is true and there is no `personas.review_triager` entry: a `persona_settings` KeyError mid-tick, or a `resolve_profile` validation error. Pin one behaviour and add it to the AC5 tests.

findings.title: Unmet-AC cause missing from the list of cases where the triager cannot help
findings.detail: The prose lists "a `must_fix`, a surviving `fix` verdict, a synthetic `major`". SPEC-0203's `score_only` also excludes an unmet AC (a hard stop that can coexist with real findings). The predicate is correct because it relies on `score_only`. Add "an unmet AC" to the list so the prose matches, and add an unmet-AC row to the AC1 truth table.

findings.title: `depends_on` omits SPEC-0201
findings.detail: The design relies on SPEC-0201's `plan_step` REVIEWING contract, the `_cap_blocks(state, profile, personas)` generalisation, `entry_run` and the clear-on-entry step 4. SPEC-0201 is only a transitive dependency through SPEC-0203, so listing it explicitly makes the ordering clearer.

findings.title: Awkward sentence about `previous_verdicts`
findings.detail: "`previous_verdicts` blanked (`_prepare_run` passes no `run.end` events for this persona, since `triage_input` already carries the verdicts)" is a run-on inside a bullet. Also say whether the triager gets the diff or gate summary, since "out of scope" and "non-defect" judgments may need the code. If it does not, state that it relies on the finding details and its read-only worktree access.
